components.note: 门 (gate) — marks gates and doors, as in 问, 间, 开; 闪 is a person 人 glimpsed through a gate: a flash, to dodge.

example.hanzi: 天空中闪过一道光。
example.pinyin: Tiānkōng zhōng shǎn guò yí dào guāng.
example.english: A beam of light flashed across the sky.
example.fact: 闪 gives 闪电 (lightning), 闪光灯 (camera flash) and 闪开 ('get out of the way'). Colloquially 闪了腰 means to throw out your back, and 闪婚 is a 'flash marriage' to someone you've known only briefly.

examples.hanzi: 夜空中的星星一闪一闪的。
examples.pinyin: Yèkōng zhōng de xīngxing yì shǎn yì shǎn de.
examples.english: The stars in the night sky twinkle.

examples.hanzi: 手机屏幕一直在闪。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī píngmù yìzhí zài shǎn.
examples.english: The phone screen keeps flickering.

components.note: 钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 钱 money, 银 silver, 钢 steel; 铁 is iron.
失 (shī) is only a loose hint for tiě.

example.hanzi: 我每天坐地铁上班。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zuò dìtiě shàngbān.
example.english: I take the subway to work every day.
example.fact: 铁 forms transport words: 铁路 (railway), 地铁 (subway), 高铁 (high-speed rail). It also means 'firm, ironclad': 铁了心 is to be totally determined, and 铁哥们 means a very close male friend.

examples.hanzi: 这个铁盒里装着很多旧照片。
examples.pinyin: Zhège tiě hé li zhuāng zhe hěn duō jiù zhàopiàn.
examples.english: This iron box holds a lot of old photos.

examples.hanzi: 这条铁路连接两座城市。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo tiělù liánjiē liǎng zuò chéngshì.
examples.english: This railway connects two cities.

components.note: 旡 (turned-away person) — someone turning from the food 皀 after eating: already done. Compare 即, who is just about to eat.

example.hanzi: 既然你来了,就一起吃饭吧。
example.pinyin: Jìrán nǐ lái le, jiù yìqǐ chīfàn ba.
example.english: Since you're here, let's eat together.
example.fact: 既 gives two useful patterns: 既然…就… ('since… then…') and 既…又… ('both… and…'), as in 既便宜又好吃 (both cheap and tasty). Its sibling 即 shows a person facing the food instead.

examples.hanzi: 他既聪明又努力。
examples.pinyin: Tā jì cōngming yòu nǔlì.
examples.english: He is both smart and hardworking.

examples.hanzi: 既然下雨了,我们就别去了。
examples.pinyin: Jìrán xià yǔ le, wǒmen jiù bié qù le.
examples.english: Since it's raining, let's not go.

components.note: 幸 (luck) — often read as an old picture of shackles; 'luck' is escaping punishment. The dictionary story (one alive 土, one dead 干) is a memory aid.
土 (earth) — the top. Memory aid: the one standing on solid ground 土 is the lucky one — 幸运, 幸福.
子 (child) — children and offspring: 孩 child, 学 study, 孙 grandchild; 存 means to keep or survive.
才 (cái) is only a loose sound hint for cún.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 这次事故只有三名幸存者。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì shìgù zhǐyǒu sān míng xìngcúnzhě.
example.english: There were only three survivors of this accident.
example.fact: 者 is one of Mandarin's most productive suffixes for "the one who does X," turning a verb phrase into a role — 记者 ("journalist," 记 "to record"), 作者 ("author," 作 "to make") — so 幸存者, built on 幸存 ("to luckily survive"), literally reads "one who luckily survived."

examples.hanzi: 他是这次空难中唯一的幸存者。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zhè cì kōngnàn zhōng wéiyī de xìngcúnzhě.
examples.english: He was the only survivor of this plane crash.

examples.hanzi: 救援队正在寻找幸存者。
examples.pinyin: Jiùyuánduì zhèngzài xúnzhǎo xìngcúnzhě.
examples.english: The rescue team is searching for survivors.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 土 is earth, as in 地, 城; 增 is piling earth higher, then increasing.
曾 (céng) — near sound — 增 is zēng; 曾 also sounds out 赠 zèng and 憎 zēng.
力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.

example.hanzi: 今年公司的员工人数增加了很多。
example.pinyin: Jīnnián gōngsī de yuángōng rénshù zēngjiā le hěn duō.
example.english: The company's staff numbers increased a lot this year.
example.fact: 增加 pairs naturally with countable, discrete quantities — 人数增加 ("the headcount increased"), 收入增加 ("income increased") — while its cousin 增长 leans toward rates and trends, as in 经济增长 ("economic growth"); swapping the two is a common slip when learners write about statistics.

examples.hanzi: 这个月的销量增加了百分之十。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè de xiāoliàng zēngjiā le bǎi fēn zhī shí.
examples.english: This month's sales increased by ten percent.

examples.hanzi: 多吃蔬菜可以增加身体的营养。
examples.pinyin: Duō chī shūcài kěyǐ zēngjiā shēntǐ de yíngyǎng.
examples.english: Eating more vegetables can add to your body's nutrition.

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 在所有的学生当中,她的成绩最好。
example.pinyin: Zài suǒyǒu de xuésheng dāngzhōng, tā de chéngjì zuì hǎo.
example.english: Among all the students, she has the best grades.
example.fact: 当中 attaches after a noun phrase in the frame "在...当中" ("among/in the midst of...") much like a postposition — a more formal, literary-leaning alternative to the plainer 中 or 之中 in the same slot.

examples.hanzi: 当中有一个人我不认识。
examples.pinyin: Dāngzhōng yǒu yí ge rén wǒ bú rènshi.
examples.english: There is one person among them I don't know.

examples.hanzi: 他们在人群当中找了很久。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài rénqún dāngzhōng zhǎo le hěn jiǔ.
examples.english: They searched among the crowd for a long time.

components.note: 牙 (tooth) — a picture of interlocking teeth; 牙 also sounds out 芽 yá and 讶 yà.
止 (zhǐ) — near sound — 齿 is chǐ; the lower part pictures teeth in a mouth, and 齿 is the tooth radical.

example.hanzi: 医生检查了我的牙齿。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le wǒ de yáchǐ.
example.english: The doctor examined my teeth.
example.fact: 齿, whose own shape pictures an open mouth (凵) with rows of teeth inside, is the more literary, classical word for "tooth"; 牙 is the everyday colloquial one (牙医 "dentist," 牙刷 "toothbrush") — 牙齿 pairs a classical-register word with a colloquial one into a single neutral, standard term.

examples.hanzi: 每天早晚都要刷牙，保护牙齿。
examples.pinyin: Měi tiān zǎowǎn dōu yào shuā yá, bǎohù yáchǐ.
examples.english: Brush your teeth morning and night to protect them.

examples.hanzi: 他的牙齿又白又整齐。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yáchǐ yòu bái yòu zhěngqí.
examples.english: His teeth are white and even.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike; 攴) — hitting actions, as in 收 gather, 教 teach, 改 change.
高 (gāo) is a loose sound clue for qiāo; it also appears in 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.

example.hanzi: 请先敲门。
example.pinyin: Qǐng xiān qiāo mén.
example.english: Please knock on the door first.
example.fact: 敲 is the standard verb for knocking: 敲门 (knock on a door), 敲键盘 (tap a keyboard). 敲定 means to settle or finalize, and 敲竹杠 is slang for overcharging.

examples.hanzi: 他用锤子敲了几下钉子。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng chuízi qiāo le jǐ xià dīngzi.
examples.english: He hit the nail a few times with a hammer.

examples.hanzi: 他在电脑上敲了一封邮件。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài diànnǎo shang qiāo le yì fēng yóujiàn.
examples.english: He typed out an email on the computer.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 肚 belly, 脚 foot, 脸 face, 胖 fat; 脑 is the brain.
The right half shows hair over a skull and also sounds out 恼 nǎo and 瑙 nǎo.

example.hanzi: 他做生意很有头脑。
example.pinyin: Tā zuò shēngyi hěn yǒu tóunǎo.
example.english: He has a real head for business.
example.fact: 头脑 usually names mental capacity or wits — 有头脑 ("sharp, clever") — rather than the literal anatomical organ, which Mandarin more often calls 大脑 in a medical context; it's closer to English "brains" in "she's got brains" than to the physical brain itself.

examples.hanzi: 她很有头脑，一下子就想出了办法。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn yǒu tóunǎo, yíxiàzi jiù xiǎng chū le bànfǎ.
examples.english: She is sharp-minded and thought of a solution right away.

examples.hanzi: 做事要用头脑，不能冲动。
examples.pinyin: Zuò shì yào yòng tóunǎo, bù néng chōngdòng.
examples.english: Use your head when doing things; don't be impulsive.

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 任 is a duty a person bears.
壬 (rén) gives the same sound, different tone; also in 妊 rèn.

example.hanzi: 她被任命为部门主任。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi rènmìng wéi bùmén zhǔrèn.
example.english: She was appointed director of the department.
example.fact: 主 ("main, master") plus 任 (亻"person" plus the phonetic 壬, "to bear a duty") builds "the one who bears the main responsibility" — 主任 is an extremely common title across Chinese schools, hospitals, and government offices, roughly matching English "director" or "head."

examples.hanzi: 主任正在办公室开会。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔrèn zhèngzài bàngōngshì kāihuì.
examples.english: The director is having a meeting in the office.

examples.hanzi: 李主任明天要去上海出差。
examples.pinyin: Lǐ zhǔrèn míngtiān yào qù Shànghǎi chūchāi.
examples.english: Director Li is going to Shanghai on a business trip tomorrow.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread; traditional 糸) — marks thread and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 线 line; 绕 is winding thread around, then going around.
尧 (yáo) — loose sound hint (rào vs yáo); same part in 晓 xiǎo and 烧 shāo.

example.hanzi: 这条路要绕很远。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù yào rào hěn yuǎn.
example.english: You have to go a long way around on this road.
example.fact: 绕 means to circle, wind or take a detour: 绕路 (detour), 围绕 (revolve around), 绕口令 (tongue twister). 绕圈子 literally 'go in circles' means to beat around the bush.

examples.hanzi: 我们绕着公园走了一圈。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen rào zhe gōngyuán zǒu le yì quān.
examples.english: We walked a lap around the park.

examples.hanzi: 你说话别绕圈子。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuōhuà bié rào quānzi.
examples.english: Don't beat around the bush.

meanings: variant of 直升機|直升机[zhi2 sheng1 ji1]

components.note: 目 (eye) — sighting along a straight line. 直 also sounds out 值 zhí and 植 zhí.
十 (ten/cross) — the visible part; 升 once was a ladle measuring grain, then 'to rise'. The shape does not explain this. Memory aid: a ladle lifted high.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 一架直升机在城市上空飞行。
example.pinyin: Yí jià zhíshēngjī zài chéngshì shàngkōng fēixíng.
example.english: A helicopter is flying over the city.
example.fact: 直升机 literally reads "straight-rising machine," describing exactly what makes it different from 飞机 ("flying machine," any airplane): a helicopter takes off straight up, needing no runway.

examples.hanzi: 直升机降落在医院的楼顶上。
examples.pinyin: Zhíshēngjī jiàngluò zài yīyuàn de lóudǐng shang.
examples.english: The helicopter landed on the hospital roof.

examples.hanzi: 救援人员乘直升机赶到了现场。
examples.pinyin: Jiùyuán rényuán chéng zhíshēngjī gǎn dào le xiànchǎng.
examples.english: Rescue workers rushed to the scene by helicopter.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 渴 is thirst, a need for water.
曷 (hé) — near sound — 渴 is kě; 曷 also sounds out 喝 hē.
亡 (wáng) is a close sound clue for wàng; it also sounds out 忘 wàng (forget) and 网 wǎng.
月 (moon) — to gaze up at the moon, so to look into the distance, then to hope.

example.hanzi: 他渴望能出国留学。
example.pinyin: Tā kěwàng néng chūguó liúxué.
example.english: He longs to study abroad.
example.fact: 渴 ("thirst," built on the water radical 氵) plus 望 ("to gaze into the distance, to hope") combine physical thirst with a long stare toward the horizon — a vivid metaphor for craving, paralleling English's own "to thirst for" knowledge or freedom.

examples.hanzi: 很多年轻人渴望自由。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō niánqīng rén kěwàng zìyóu.
examples.english: Many young people long for freedom.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们渴望得到父母的关心。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen kěwàng dédào fùmǔ de guānxīn.
examples.english: Children long for their parents' care.

components.note: 页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 颜; 领 is the neck and then to lead.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 领 is lǐng; 令 also sounds out 龄 líng and 铃 líng.

example.hanzi: 老师领孩子们过马路。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī lǐng háizimen guò mǎlù.
example.english: The teacher leads the children across the road.
example.fact: 领 began as 'neck' and extended to collar (衣领, 领带 for necktie), to lead (带领, 领导) and to receive (领奖, 领钱). Leading people is like grabbing them by the collar.

examples.hanzi: 他的衬衫领子有点脏。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chènshān lǐngzi yǒudiǎn zāng.
examples.english: His shirt collar is a bit dirty.

examples.hanzi: 导游领着我们参观了博物馆。
examples.pinyin: Dǎoyóu lǐng zhe wǒmen cānguān le bówùguǎn.
examples.english: The guide led us around the museum.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood and trees, as in 树, 林, 桌: 校 first meant a wooden frame or restraint.
交 (jiāo) is a close sound clue for xiào; 交 also in 较 jiào and 校 xiào.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 校长在开学典礼上讲话。
example.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng zài kāixué diǎnlǐ shàng jiǎnghuà.
example.english: The principal spoke at the opening ceremony.
example.fact: 校 has two readings — xiào ("school") in 校长 and 学校, and jiào ("to proofread, to compare") in 校对 ("to proofread") — a common trap for learners since the character looks identical in both words.

examples.hanzi: 校长邀请家长来参观学校。
examples.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng yāoqǐng jiāzhǎng lái cānguān xuéxiào.
examples.english: The principal invited parents to visit the school.

examples.hanzi: 我们校长每天早上都站在门口迎接学生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiàozhǎng měi tiān zǎoshang dōu zhàn zài ménkǒu yíngjiē xuésheng.
examples.english: Our principal stands at the gate every morning to greet the students.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
手 (hand) — the bottom form shows a hand; 拿 is two hands closing 合 on something: to take hold.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.hanzi: 我朋友明年要去加拿大留学。
example.pinyin: Wǒ péngyou míngnián yào qù Jiānádà liúxué.
example.english: My friend is going to study abroad in Canada next year.
example.fact: 加拿大 is a phonetic transliteration of "Canada" with no meaning behind the characters themselves — 加 ("add"), 拿 ("take"), and 大 ("big") were chosen purely for their sounds jiā-ná-dà, a common strategy for rendering foreign place names into Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 加拿大的冬天很长，雪也很多。
examples.pinyin: Jiānádà de dōngtiān hěn cháng, xuě yě hěn duō.
examples.english: Winters in Canada are long and there is a lot of snow.

examples.hanzi: 他在加拿大住了五年，英语说得很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài Jiānádà zhù le wǔ nián, Yīngyǔ shuō de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He lived in Canada for five years and speaks good English.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑, 驶; 驾 is to harness a horse, then drive.
加 (jiā) — same sound, different tone — 驾 is jià; 加 also sounds out 架 jià.
马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑, 驾; 驶 is to drive swiftly.
史 (shǐ) — same sound — 驶 is shǐ, like 史.

example.hanzi: 他正在学习驾驶飞机。
example.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài xuéxí jiàshǐ fēijī.
example.english: He is learning to fly (pilot) an airplane.
example.fact: Both characters in 驾驶 carry the horse radical 马 — a reminder that the word predates automobiles and airplanes, having first described controlling a horse-drawn carriage before broadening to any vehicle.

examples.hanzi: 开车时不要玩手机，驾驶要小心。
examples.pinyin: Kāi chē shí bú yào wán shǒujī, jiàshǐ yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: Don't play with your phone while driving; drive carefully.

examples.hanzi: 他有十年的驾驶经验。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu shí nián de jiàshǐ jīngyàn.
examples.english: He has ten years of driving experience.

components.note: 玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 医生全力抢救伤者。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng quánlì qiǎngjiù shāngzhě.
example.english: The doctors worked with all their strength to save the injured.
example.fact: 全力 almost always appears as an adverb right before a verb (全力支持 "fully support") rather than standing alone as a noun — the set four-character idiom 全力以赴 ("to go all out") is one of the most common ways to build on it.

examples.hanzi: 我们会全力支持你的决定。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen huì quánlì zhīchí nǐ de juédìng.
examples.english: We will fully support your decision.

examples.hanzi: 他全力跑向终点。
examples.pinyin: Tā quánlì pǎo xiàng zhōngdiǎn.
examples.english: He ran toward the finish line with all his strength.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 溜 is sliding and slipping, as water does.
留 (liú) — close sound: 溜 liū. 留 also sounds out 榴 liú.

example.hanzi: 他偷偷溜出去了。
example.pinyin: Tā tōutōu liū chūqù le.
example.english: He sneaked out.
example.fact: 溜 is about moving smoothly or stealthily: 溜走 (slip away), 溜冰 (ice skate), 溜达 (to stroll). 滑溜 describes something slippery or smooth.

examples.hanzi: 他在冰面上溜了一圈。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bīngmiàn shang liū le yì quān.
examples.english: He glided a lap on the ice.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们去公园溜达溜达。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù gōngyuán liūda liūda.
examples.english: On the weekend we'll go stroll in the park.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 围; 团 is a round group. Its traditional form had 專 as sound, like 转 zhuǎn and 传 chuán.
米 (rice) — grain and food, as in 粉 powder, 糕 cake, 精 refined: 糟 is dregs of fermented rice, then spoiled.
曹 (cáo) is a close sound clue for zāo; 曹 also in 遭 zāo and 槽 cáo.

example.hanzi: 房间里被弄得一团糟。
example.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ bèi nòng de yìtuánzāo.
example.english: The room was made into a complete mess.
example.fact: 团 contributes its sense of a rounded, clumped mass (also seen in 面团 "dough" and 主席团 "presidium") to 一团糟 — literally "one clump of dregs," picturing disorder as something balled up together rather than merely scattered about.

examples.hanzi: 我的桌子一团糟，找不到东西了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de zhuōzi yì tuán zāo, zhǎo bú dào dōngxi le.
examples.english: My desk is a complete mess and I can't find anything.

examples.hanzi: 会议开得一团糟，什么也没决定。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì kāi de yì tuán zāo, shénme yě méi juédìng.
examples.english: The meeting was a mess and nothing was decided.

components.note: 大 (big) — an extra stroke below emphasises it: bigger than big, too much. 太 also sounds out 泰 tài.
穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.

example.hanzi: 中国的太空计划发展很快。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó de tàikōng jìhuà fāzhǎn hěn kuài.
example.english: China's space program is developing quickly.
example.fact: 太空 literally means "extremely empty" (太 "extremely" + 空 "empty, sky") — the same 空 that means "empty" in 空房间 ("empty room") extends naturally to the vast emptiness beyond the atmosphere.

examples.hanzi: 宇航员在太空里生活了半年。
examples.pinyin: Yǔhángyuán zài tàikōng lǐ shēnghuó le bàn nián.
examples.english: The astronaut lived in space for half a year.

examples.hanzi: 我想坐飞船去太空看看。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zuò fēichuán qù tàikōng kànkan.
examples.english: I want to take a spaceship to see outer space.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.

example.hanzi: 他昨天生病了,没来上班。
example.pinyin: Tā zuótiān shēngbìng le, méi lái shàngbān.
example.english: He got sick yesterday and didn't come to work.
example.fact: 生病 is a verb-object compound built from 生 ("to give rise to, to produce") + 病 ("illness") — literally "to produce sickness" — which is why 病 can still be pulled out and used on its own as a noun (他的病 "his illness") even though 生病 has become the fixed verb for "to fall ill."

examples.hanzi: 我昨天生病了，一直在家休息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān shēngbìng le, yìzhí zài jiā xiūxi.
examples.english: I got sick yesterday and rested at home all day.

examples.hanzi: 天气变冷了，小心别生病。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì biàn lěng le, xiǎoxīn bié shēngbìng.
examples.english: The weather has turned cold, so be careful not to get sick.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 适 is to go to what suits you. 舌 is a simplification stand-in, not a real clue.
广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).

example.hanzi: 新学生需要时间适应新环境。
example.pinyin: Xīn xuésheng xūyào shíjiān shìyìng xīn huánjìng.
example.english: New students need time to adapt to a new environment.
example.fact: 应 here is read yìng ("to respond, to react"), the same reading it takes in 应付 (also in this batch) and 反应 ("reaction") — not the yīng reading used in 应该 ("should"), a distinction worth tracking since the character 应 covers both senses depending on tone.

examples.hanzi: 刚搬到这里，我还不适应这里的天气。
examples.pinyin: Gāng bān dào zhèlǐ, wǒ hái bú shìyìng zhèlǐ de tiānqì.
examples.english: I just moved here and haven't gotten used to the weather yet.

examples.hanzi: 孩子很快就适应了新学校。
examples.pinyin: Háizi hěn kuài jiù shìyìng le xīn xuéxiào.
examples.english: The child quickly adapted to the new school.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 艾 is mugwort, a medicinal herb, as in 草 grass, 药 medicine.
乂 (yì) is only a loose sound clue for ài.

example.hanzi: 端午节人们会挂艾草。
example.pinyin: Duānwǔ Jié rénmen huì guà àicǎo.
example.english: People hang mugwort during the Dragon Boat Festival.
example.fact: 艾 is mugwort, burned in moxibustion (艾灸) and hung on doors at the Dragon Boat Festival to ward off evil. It is also a surname and used in transliterations such as 艾滋病 (AIDS).

examples.hanzi: 艾草有一股特别的香味。
examples.pinyin: Àicǎo yǒu yì gǔ tèbié de xiāngwèi.
examples.english: Mugwort has a special fragrance.

examples.hanzi: 他有一个同学姓艾。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu yí ge tóngxué xìng Ài.
examples.english: He has a classmate whose surname is Ai.

components.note: 取 (qǔ, take) is a loose sound clue for jù; the part below shows people gathered together.

example.hanzi: 周末朋友们聚在一起吃饭。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò péngyoumen jù zài yìqǐ chīfàn.
example.english: On the weekend, friends gather for a meal.
example.fact: 聚 is for people or things coming together: 聚会 (get-together), 聚餐 (group meal), 团聚 (reunion), 聚焦 (to focus). Its opposite is 散 (sàn), and 聚散 means meeting and parting.

examples.hanzi: 好久不见,我们找时间聚一聚吧。
examples.pinyin: Hǎojiǔ bú jiàn, wǒmen zhǎo shíjiān jù yi jù ba.
examples.english: Long time no see, let's find time to get together.

examples.hanzi: 同学聚会在周六晚上。
examples.pinyin: Tóngxué jùhuì zài zhōuliù wǎnshang.
examples.english: The class reunion is on Saturday night.

components.note: 广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 付 is handing 寸 something to a person.
付 (fù) is also the sound in 附 fù, 府 fǔ, 符 fú and 腐 fǔ.

example.hanzi: 面对突然的问题,他很难应付。
example.pinyin: Miànduì tūrán de wèntí, tā hěn nán yìngfu.
example.english: Faced with the sudden problem, he found it hard to cope.
example.fact: 应付 can carry a slightly negative shade beyond a neutral "to deal with" — 应付了事 is a set phrase meaning to handle something half-heartedly just to get it over with, so 应付 alone can hint at reluctant or perfunctory effort depending on context.

examples.hanzi: 这么多工作，我一个人应付不过来。
examples.pinyin: Zhème duō gōngzuò, wǒ yí ge rén yìngfu bú guòlái.
examples.english: With this much work, I can't cope on my own.

examples.hanzi: 他随便说了几句话来应付客人。
examples.pinyin: Tā suíbiàn shuō le jǐ jù huà lái yìngfu kèrén.
examples.english: He said a few casual words to get through the guests.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.
口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 请不要在这里放置私人物品。
example.pinyin: Qǐng búyào zài zhèlǐ fàngzhì sīrén wùpǐn.
example.english: Please do not place personal belongings here.
example.fact: 品 by itself already means "item, product" and stacks three 口 ("mouth") shapes — traditionally read as many people judging or grading something together — which is also why 品 alone can mean "quality, grade," as in 人品 ("moral character").

examples.hanzi: 请保管好你的贵重物品。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎoguǎn hǎo nǐ de guìzhòng wùpǐn.
examples.english: Please take good care of your valuables.

examples.hanzi: 这些物品都是免费提供的。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē wùpǐn dōu shì miǎnfèi tígōng de.
examples.english: All these items are provided free of charge.

components.note: 土 (earth) — soil and land: 地, 场, 块; 坏 first meant to collapse, as of a wall of earth.
不 (bù) is only a stand-in for the old sound part 褱 (huái); a loose clue for huài.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 电影里的坏人最后被警察抓住了。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de huàirén zuìhòu bèi jǐngchá zhuāzhù le.
example.english: In the end, the villain in the movie was caught by the police.
example.fact: 坏人 simply pairs 坏 ("bad, broken") with 人 ("person") — about as transparent as Chinese compounds get — and it names a moral judgment about someone's character, distinct from the more casual, almost playful insult 坏蛋 ("bad egg").

examples.hanzi: 他看起来很凶，但不是坏人。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlái hěn xiōng, dàn bú shì huàirén.
examples.english: He looks fierce, but he isn't a bad person.

examples.hanzi: 小朋友，不要跟陌生人走，他们可能是坏人。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎopéngyou, bú yào gēn mòshēngrén zǒu, tāmen kěnéng shì huàirén.
examples.english: Kids, don't go with strangers; they might be bad people.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — marks cutting and dividing, as in 别, 刻, 划; 列 is to split into rows, hence a line or list.
歹 (bone, death) — marks death and decay, as in 死, 残; 列 liè itself also sounds out 烈 liè and 裂 liè.

example.hanzi: 请把名字列在这张表上。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ míngzi liè zài zhè zhāng biǎo shàng.
example.english: Please list the names on this table.
example.fact: 列 means to line up or list: 列表 (list), 列出 (list out), 排列 (to arrange). It is also the measure word for trains: 一列火车. 列车 is a formal word for a train.

examples.hanzi: 他把要买的东西列了一张清单。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ yào mǎi de dōngxi liè le yì zhāng qīngdān.
examples.english: He made a list of the things to buy.

examples.hanzi: 一列火车从山洞里开了出来。
examples.pinyin: Yí liè huǒchē cóng shāndòng li kāi le chūlái.
examples.english: A train came out of the tunnel.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 湿 is wet or damp.
显 (xiǎn) — loose sound hint (shī vs xiǎn).

example.hanzi: 我的衣服湿了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de yīfu shī le.
example.english: My clothes are wet.
example.fact: 湿 gives 潮湿 (humid), 湿度 (humidity), 湿巾 (wet wipe) and 湿透 (soaked). In traditional Chinese medicine, 湿气 ('dampness') is a common idea in wellness advice.

examples.hanzi: 外面下雨,我的鞋都湿了。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn xià yǔ, wǒ de xié dōu shī le.
examples.english: It's raining outside and my shoes are soaked.

examples.hanzi: 梅雨季节空气很潮湿。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǔ jìjié kōngqì hěn cháoshī.
examples.english: The air is very humid in the rainy season.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 撑 is propping up or holding open.
掌 (zhǎng) — close sound: 撑 chēng. 掌 also sounds out 堂 táng and 常 cháng.

example.hanzi: 他用手撑着头。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒu chēng zhe tóu.
example.english: He rests his head on his hand.
example.fact: 撑 means to hold up or push with a pole: 撑伞 (hold up an umbrella), 支撑 (support), 撑船 (pole a boat). Colloquially 吃撑了 or 撑死了 means 'stuffed from eating too much'.

examples.hanzi: 他撑着雨伞走在雨里。
examples.pinyin: Tā chēng zhe yǔsǎn zǒu zài yǔ lǐ.
examples.english: He walks in the rain holding an umbrella.

examples.hanzi: 吃得太多,肚子都撑了。
examples.pinyin: Chī de tài duō, dùzi dōu chēng le.
examples.english: I ate too much and my stomach is stuffed.

components.note: 殳 (strike) — 殳 is a hand striking with a tool, as in 殴, 段; 毁 is to wreck.
火 (fire) — 火 is fire, as in 烧, 灯, 炒; 灭 covers a fire with a stroke 一 to put it out.

example.hanzi: 一场大火几乎毁灭了整座森林。
example.pinyin: Yì chǎng dàhuǒ jīhū huǐmiè le zhěng zuò sēnlín.
example.english: A huge fire almost destroyed the entire forest.
example.fact: 毁灭 doubles up two independent "destruction" verbs — 毁 ("to smash, to wreck") and 灭 ("to extinguish, to wipe out," literally a flame smothered under a cover) — into one intensified word for total, often irreversible destruction.

examples.hanzi: 战争会毁灭一座城市。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng huì huǐmiè yí zuò chéngshì.
examples.english: War can destroy a city.

examples.hanzi: 他的一次错误决定毁灭了整个公司。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yí cì cuòwù juédìng huǐmiè le zhěnggè gōngsī.
examples.english: One wrong decision of his ruined the whole company.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话; 诅 is a spoken curse.
且 (qiě) — near sound — 诅 is zǔ; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ and 组 zǔ.
口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫; 咒 is a curse spoken aloud.

example.hanzi: 她诅咒那个骗她钱的人。
example.pinyin: Tā zǔzhòu nàge piàn tā qián de rén.
example.english: She cursed the person who swindled her out of money.
example.fact: Both halves point to speech: 诅 carries the 讠 ("speech") radical, and 咒 is traditionally analyzed as two stacked 口 ("mouth," suggesting chanting) above 兄 — together underscoring that 诅咒 specifically means invoking a curse through spoken ritual words, not just a casual insult.

examples.hanzi: 那个人诅咒了我们，说我们不会成功。
examples.pinyin: Nàge rén zǔzhòu le wǒmen, shuō wǒmen bú huì chénggōng.
examples.english: That person cursed us, saying we would never succeed.

examples.hanzi: 童话里的巫婆诅咒了公主。
examples.pinyin: Tónghuà lǐ de wūpó zǔzhòu le gōngzhǔ.
examples.english: The witch in the fairy tale cursed the princess.

meanings: expression or emotion showing in one's eyes

components.note: 目 (eye) — sight, as in 看, 睛, 睡.
艮 (gèn) is a loose sound clue for yǎn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 很 hěn and 根 gēn.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.

example.hanzi: 她的眼神里充满了担心。
example.pinyin: Tā de yǎnshén lǐ chōngmǎn le dānxīn.
example.english: Her eyes were full of worry.
example.fact: 神 here keeps its core sense of "spirit, vitality" rather than its more common "god, deity" meaning — 眼神 literally reads as "eye spirit," the animating look that shows through someone's eyes, the same 神 found in 精神 ("spirit, energy").

examples.hanzi: 他用坚定的眼神看着我。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng jiāndìng de yǎnshén kàn zhe wǒ.
examples.english: He looked at me with a firm gaze.

examples.hanzi: 从她的眼神里，我知道她在说谎。
examples.pinyin: Cóng tā de yǎnshén lǐ, wǒ zhīdào tā zài shuōhuǎng.
examples.english: From the look in her eyes, I knew she was lying.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — a picture of a crawling worm; as a radical it marks insects and creepy-crawlies, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蜘 spider, 蛇 snake.

example.hanzi: 树上有很多虫子。
example.pinyin: Shù shàng yǒu hěn duō chóngzi.
example.english: There are many bugs in the tree.
example.fact: 虫 is the simplified form of 蟲, which stacked three 虫 for 'many crawling creatures'. It is the radical in 蛇, 蚂蚁 and 蝴蝶. Add 子 for 虫子 (bug), 昆虫 (insect) and 害虫 (pest).

examples.hanzi: 夏天晚上有很多小虫子。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǎnshang yǒu hěn duō xiǎo chóngzi.
examples.english: There are lots of little bugs on summer nights.

examples.hanzi: 苹果里有一条小虫。
examples.pinyin: Píngguǒ li yǒu yì tiáo xiǎo chóng.
examples.english: There is a little worm in the apple.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — words passed down through ten 十 generations of mouths — old; 古 also sounds out 姑 gū and 故 gù.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: a strange feeling.
圣 here is not the "sage" word; it is only a loose sound clue for guài.

example.hanzi: 这座老房子看起来很古怪。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò lǎo fángzi kàn qǐlai hěn gǔguài.
example.english: This old house looks very strange.
example.fact: 古怪 pairs 古 ("old, ancient") with 怪 ("strange, odd") — something unusually old-fashioned or out of step with the times reads as simply "strange," a small window into how "outdated" and "odd" overlap in the word's origin.

examples.hanzi: 他是个古怪的人，常常自言自语。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge gǔguài de rén, chángcháng zìyán zìyǔ.
examples.english: He is an eccentric person who often talks to himself.

examples.hanzi: 晚上，窗外传来一阵古怪的声音。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang, chuāngwài chuánlái yí zhèn gǔguài de shēngyīn.
examples.english: At night, a strange sound came from outside the window.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 买, 费, 贵; 财 is wealth.
才 (cái) — same sound — 财 is cái, like 才; 才 also sounds out 材 cái.
生 (birth) — traditional 產 was 生 (birth) topped by 彦 for sound; the idea is giving birth, so bringing forth, as in 生产 and 产生.

example.hanzi: 他把所有财产都留给了孩子。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ suǒyǒu cáichǎn dōu liú gěi le háizi.
example.english: He left all his property to his children.
example.fact: 财 carries the 贝 ("cowrie shell") radical seen across many wealth-related characters (贵 "expensive," 购 "to purchase," 贫 "poor") — a fossil of the era when shells functioned as currency in ancient China, long before coined money.

examples.hanzi: 这笔财产应该由两个孩子平分。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ cáichǎn yīnggāi yóu liǎng ge háizi píngfēn.
examples.english: This property should be split equally between the two children.

examples.hanzi: 保护个人财产是每个人的权利。
examples.pinyin: Bǎohù gèrén cáichǎn shì měi ge rén de quánlì.
examples.english: Protecting personal property is everyone's right.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 任 is a duty a person bears.
壬 (rén) gives the same sound, different tone; also in 妊 rèn.

example.hanzi: 他是我们的班主任。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen de bānzhǔrèn.
example.english: He is our class teacher.
example.fact: 任 builds 责任 (responsibility), 任务 (task), 任何 (any), 信任 (trust) and 任性 (willful). As a surname it is read Rén.

examples.hanzi: 他任经理已经五年了。
examples.pinyin: Tā rèn jīnglǐ yǐjīng wǔ nián le.
examples.english: He has served as manager for five years.

examples.hanzi: 照顾孩子是父母的责任。
examples.pinyin: Zhàogù háizi shì fùmǔ de zérèn.
examples.english: Taking care of children is the parents' responsibility.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions of striking or acting: 教, 放, 改, 政; 攻 is to attack.
工 (gōng) sounds exactly like 攻; also in 功 gōng, 红 hóng, 空 kōng.

example.hanzi: 敌军决定在黎明前发起进攻。
example.pinyin: Díjūn juédìng zài límíng qián fāqǐ jìngōng.
example.english: The enemy army decided to launch an attack before dawn.
example.fact: 进攻 literally combines "to advance" (进) with "to strike" (攻) — a transparent military compound that extends naturally to sports commentary, where 进攻 is simply the standard word for "offense" as opposed to 防守 ("defense").

examples.hanzi: 我们的球队开始向对方进攻。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de qiúduì kāishǐ xiàng duìfāng jìngōng.
examples.english: Our team started to attack the other side.

examples.hanzi: 进攻是最好的防守。
examples.pinyin: Jìngōng shì zuì hǎo de fángshǒu.
examples.english: Attack is the best defense.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — marks cutting and dividing, as in 别, 刻; 剂 is a measured dose, as in 药剂 medicine.
齐 (qí) — loose sound hint (jì vs qí); 齐 also means even, fitting a measured dose.

example.hanzi: 医生给我开了一剂药。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi wǒ kāi le yí jì yào.
example.english: The doctor prescribed me a dose of medicine.
example.fact: 剂 is a measure word for doses of herbal medicine (一剂中药) and appears in 药剂 (pharmaceutical), 试剂 (reagent) and 针剂 (injection). 强心剂 is literally a 'heart tonic', used figuratively for a morale boost.

examples.hanzi: 医生开了一种退烧剂。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng kāi le yì zhǒng tuìshāojì.
examples.english: The doctor prescribed a fever reducer.

examples.hanzi: 这瓶消毒剂要放在孩子拿不到的地方。
examples.pinyin: Zhè píng xiāodújì yào fàng zài háizi ná bu dào de dìfang.
examples.english: Keep this disinfectant where children can't reach it.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.

example.hanzi: 他是我的好伙伴。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de hǎo huǒbàn.
example.english: He is my good partner.
example.fact: 伙 builds 伙伴 (partner), 同伙 (accomplice) and 伙食 (meals served in a group kitchen). It is also a measure word for groups of people: 一伙人, often with a faintly negative tone, like 'a gang'.

examples.hanzi: 他们是一伙好朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì yì huǒ hǎo péngyou.
examples.english: They are a group of good friends.

examples.hanzi: 这个小伙子很能干。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎohuǒzi hěn nénggàn.
examples.english: This young man is very capable.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.
而 (and, but) — oldest form is a beard (compare 须 xū, beard), later borrowed for the conjunction; 而 survives in 耐 nài.

example.hanzi: 他很努力,然而结果并不理想。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn nǔlì, rán'ér jiéguǒ bìng bù lǐxiǎng.
example.english: He worked very hard; however, the result wasn't ideal.
example.fact: 然而 sits at the more formal, written end of Chinese's "but" words — closer in weight to 但是 than to the casual spoken 不过 — which is why it shows up constantly in essays and news reports but can sound a touch stiff in casual conversation.

examples.hanzi: 这个办法很简单，然而很有效。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ hěn jiǎndān, rán'ér hěn yǒuxiào.
examples.english: This method is simple, yet very effective.

examples.hanzi: 我以为她会生气，然而她只是笑了笑。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐwéi tā huì shēngqì, rán'ér tā zhǐshì xiào le xiào.
examples.english: I thought she would be angry, but she just smiled.

meanings: to go to a lot of trouble

components.note: 辛 (bitter) — 辛 pictures a sharp tool once used to mark offenders; it means bitter and laborious, as in 辛苦, and is part of 辣 and 辞.
艹 (grass, plants) — plants and herbs: 花 flower, 草 grass, 茶 tea; 苦 first named a bitter herb.
古 (gǔ) is a loose clue for kǔ — see also 枯 kū and 姑 gū.

example.hanzi: 谢谢你,这段时间辛苦你了。
example.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ, zhè duàn shíjiān xīnkǔ nǐ le.
example.english: Thank you, you've worked hard this whole time.
example.fact: 辛苦你了 is a fixed, almost ritual phrase Chinese speakers use to acknowledge someone else's effort on their behalf — closer to "thanks for all your hard work" than a word-for-word translation of "bitter and hard," and it's commonly said to service staff, colleagues, or family with no exact English equivalent.

examples.hanzi: 工作了一整天，你一定很辛苦吧？
examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò le yì zhěng tiān, nǐ yídìng hěn xīnkǔ ba?
examples.english: After working all day, you must be tired, right?

examples.hanzi: 为了养大三个孩子，妈妈吃了很多苦，很辛苦。
examples.pinyin: Wèile yǎng dà sān ge háizi, māma chī le hěn duō kǔ, hěn xīnkǔ.
examples.english: To raise three children, mom went through a lot and had a very hard time.

components.note: 水 (water) — a picture of flowing water; as a radical it appears as 氵 on the left (海, 河) or 水 at the bottom (泉, 冰).
平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.

example.hanzi: 他的英语水平提高了很多。
example.pinyin: Tā de Yīngyǔ shuǐpíng tígāo le hěn duō.
example.english: His English level has improved a lot.
example.fact: 平 alone already pictures a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — 水平 layers 水 ("water") onto that image of flatness, since still water is the clearest natural example of a perfectly level surface, and the compound then extended figuratively to mean a "standard" or "degree of skill."

examples.hanzi: 他的游泳水平和专业运动员差不多。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yóuyǒng shuǐpíng hé zhuānyè yùndòngyuán chàbuduō.
examples.english: His swimming level is about the same as a professional athlete's.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市的生活水平越来越高。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de shēnghuó shuǐpíng yuè lái yuè gāo.
examples.english: The standard of living in this city keeps rising.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
土 (earth) — 土 is earth, as in 地, 城; a mold was made of clay, so 型 is a model or type.
刑 (xíng) — same sound — 型 is xíng, like 刑.

example.hanzi: 她换了一个新发型。
example.pinyin: Tā huàn le yí gè xīn fàxíng.
example.english: She got a new hairstyle.
example.fact: 发 is one of Chinese's most notorious tone-dependent characters: read fā it means "to send out, to emit" (发送, 出发), but read fà it narrows specifically to "hair" (发型, 头发) — the simplified script merged what were two entirely different traditional characters, 發 and 髮, into this single simplified form.

examples.hanzi: 你剪了新发型，真好看！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiǎn le xīn fàxíng, zhēn hǎokàn!
examples.english: You got a new haircut. It looks great!

examples.hanzi: 这个发型很适合你的脸型。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fàxíng hěn shìhé nǐ de liǎnxíng.
examples.english: This hairstyle suits your face shape very well.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
斤 (axe) — 斤 is an axe, as in 新, 析; 断 is to cut through, shown by the axe and threads cut.

example.hanzi: 请不要打断我说话。
example.pinyin: Qǐng búyào dǎduàn wǒ shuōhuà.
example.english: Please don't interrupt me while I'm talking.
example.fact: 打断 extends 打 ("to hit") well beyond physical striking — the same "打 + verb" pattern that turns 打 into a light, almost meaningless helper verb shows up across dozens of common words (打电话 "to make a call," 打扫 "to clean") — though 打断 keeps a literal edge closer to the original "hit," since interrupting speech or breaking a bone both involve a forceful, sudden stop.

examples.hanzi: 他突然打断了我的话。
examples.pinyin: Tā tūrán dǎduàn le wǒ de huà.
examples.english: He suddenly cut off what I was saying.

examples.hanzi: 对不起，我可以打断一下吗？
examples.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ kěyǐ dǎduàn yíxià ma?
examples.english: Sorry, may I interrupt for a moment?

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.
复 (fù) sounds out 腹 fù belly and 覆 fù cover; as a word it means again or to repeat, as in 恢复, 重复.

example.hanzi: 他决定不对同事的批评进行报复。
example.pinyin: Tā juédìng bú duì tóngshì de pīpíng jìnxíng bàofù.
example.english: He decided not to retaliate against his colleague's criticism.
example.fact: 报 carries a core sense of "to repay, to respond in kind" seen across several words (报答 "to repay a kindness," 报恩 "to repay a debt of gratitude") — 报复 applies that same "paying back" logic to injury rather than kindness, framing revenge as settling a debt.

examples.hanzi: 他受到了不公平的对待，想要报复。
examples.pinyin: Tā shòudào le bù gōngpíng de duìdài, xiǎng yào bàofù.
examples.english: He was treated unfairly and wanted revenge.

examples.hanzi: 报复别人只会让事情更糟。
examples.pinyin: Bàofù biéren zhǐ huì ràng shìqing gèng zāo.
examples.english: Retaliating against others will only make things worse.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 吵 is noisy speech.
少 (shǎo) — near sound — 吵 is chǎo; 少 also sounds out 炒 chǎo and 抄 chāo.
木 (wood) — wooden things: 桌, 板, 桥; 架 is a wooden frame or rack.
加 (jiā) is a near sound match for jià; also in 驾 jià and 嘉 jiā.

example.hanzi: 他们昨天因为一点小事吵架了。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zuótiān yīnwèi yìdiǎn xiǎoshì chǎojià le.
example.english: They quarreled yesterday over a small matter.
example.fact: 架 in 吵架 keeps its sense of a "frame, structure" — the same 架 in 打架 ("to fight," literally "to hit a frame") and 架子 ("shelf, frame") — an old metaphor picturing a quarrel as something with its own scaffolding being built up between two people.

examples.hanzi: 他们为了钱的事吵架了。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen wèile qián de shì chǎojià le.
examples.english: They had a quarrel over money.

examples.hanzi: 我不想和你吵架，我们好好谈谈吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng hé nǐ chǎojià, wǒmen hǎohāo tántan ba.
examples.english: I don't want to argue with you; let's talk it through.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.hanzi: 我一整天都在写报告。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yìzhěngtiān dōu zài xiě bàogào.
example.english: I spent the whole day writing the report.
example.fact: 整 contributes "whole, complete, orderly" (as in 整齐 "neat" and 完整 "complete") — 一整天 emphasizes that literally not one hour of the day was left out, a stronger and more deliberate phrase than the plain 一天 ("one day").

examples.hanzi: 我们一整天都在海边玩。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yì zhěng tiān dōu zài hǎibiān wán.
examples.english: We played at the beach all day.

examples.hanzi: 下了一整天的雨，哪儿也不能去。
examples.pinyin: Xià le yì zhěng tiān de yǔ, nǎr yě bù néng qù.
examples.english: It rained the whole day, so we couldn't go anywhere.

components.note: 月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.
衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 这家店专卖儿童服装。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn zhuānmài értóng fúzhuāng.
example.english: This shop specializes in children's clothing.
example.fact: 服装 sits at a more formal register than the everyday 衣服 ("clothes") — 服装 shows up in store names and fashion-industry terms (服装设计 "fashion design"), while 衣服 is what people actually say when talking about the clothes in their closet.

examples.hanzi: 运动服装在三楼。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng fúzhuāng zài sān lóu.
examples.english: The sportswear is on the third floor.

examples.hanzi: 表演的时候，大家都穿着民族服装。
examples.pinyin: Biǎoyǎn de shíhou, dàjiā dōu chuān zhe mínzú fúzhuāng.
examples.english: During the performance, everyone wore ethnic costumes.
